subtitle: Hwidiem remembers its journey
answer: Adikanfo is the annual festival of the chiefs and people of Hwidiem in the Ahafo Region. It remembers the migration of their ancestors from Denkyira Ntomu to Hwidiem, with a durbar of chiefs, drumming and dancing, and offerings to the gods and ancestors. It is usually held in September.
facts: Usually September; some sources say March or April

schema.description: Festival of Hwidiem remembering the migration from Denkyira Ntomu.

sections.title: What happens
sections.html:
Adikanfo remembers how the people of Hwidiem came from Denkyira Ntomu to the town they live in now.[[1,2]] The highlight is a durbar of chiefs, with drumming and dancing; animals are sacrificed to the gods and ancestors, people wear traditional dress, and visitors are welcomed to share food and drink.[[1,2]]

Published accounts of Adikanfo are short and sometimes conflict. If you know the festival, tell us more and we’ll add it.

sections.title: When is Adikanfo?
sections.html: It is usually held in September, though some sources put it in March or April.[[1,2]] The chiefs set the days each year.

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Hwidiem is the capital of the Asutifi South District. See the Ahafo page for places nearby.
Check the dates: the traditional council sets them each year. Local radio carries the announcement.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
